title: Room and Portrait
premise: Folklorist Ivo Crane rents the last occupied house in Hollowmere, a village that sold itself decades ago to something that keeps its people alive in exchange for being remembered correctly — and never sung to twice. When Ivo's overnight audio equipment captures a second voice answering questions he never asked aloud, he realizes the house has begun treating him as the next signatory. Over one final week, Ivo must trace what the previous resident, Edith Marlow, invited in and why she never signed, holding out until sunrise on the anniversary night when the papers come due. He survives by refusing to complete the village's memory — burning his recordings and singing the songs wrong — but wakes as the only person who remembers Hollowmere at all.
about_author: Ines Galloway is the pen name of a former archivist of regional oral histories who spent years cataloguing songs no community would perform twice. They write horror about documents, houses, and the bargains hidden in both.

chapters.title: The House That Answers
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Arriving at the last inhabited house in Hollowmere, Ivo catalogs its oddities: doors that sit slightly ajar, a hallway longer at night. The landlord's solicitor mentions 'the papers' and hurries away. Emotional beat: uneasy curiosity masking seven years of rationalizations.

chapters.title: Songs Refused Twice
chapters.summary: Ivo interviews villagers for the folklore survey; every singer stops mid-verse when a line repeats. Old Tam Vetch warns that a song sung twice is an invitation. Emotional beat: professional excitement curdling into the first real dread.

chapters.title: Edith Marlow's Room
chapters.summary: Ivo discovers a sealed bedroom upstairs, wallpapered with handwritten lyrics, each verse annotated in a shaking hand: WRONG, WRONG, ALMOST. POV shifts briefly to Edith via her marginalia. Emotional beat: intimacy with a stranger's terror.

chapters.title: Baseline Recording
chapters.summary: Ivo sets recorders overnight to capture ambient sound for the archive. Playback reveals breathing that isn't his, paced to his own. He tells himself it's ductwork. Emotional beat: the comfort of explanation beginning to fray.

chapters.title: The Village That Won't Look Up
chapters.summary: Ivo walks Hollowmere mapping which houses are empty. Every resident claims neighbors moved away; every window is dark behind clean glass. A child asks if he's 'the new rememberer.' Emotional beat: isolation sharpening.

chapters.title: First Question
chapters.summary: The recording captures a second voice — dry, patient — answering a question Ivo swears he didn't ask aloud: how long he means to stay. He checks the mic for interference twice. Emotional beat: denial weaponized.

chapters.title: Tam's Debt
chapters.summary: Tam Vetch, drunk, describes the night in 1968 when the village 'signed' and the dying stopped — all of them, including those already dead. He begs Ivo not to learn the last verse of any song. Emotional beat: pity mixed with self-preservation.

chapters.title: The Papers
chapters.summary: The solicitor delivers a document to Ivo's door: a transfer of residency requiring only a signature, dated for the anniversary. Ivo reads the previous eleven names; Edith Marlow's line is blank. Emotional beat: the trap made bureaucratic and therefore worse.

chapters.title: Wrong, Wrong, Almost
chapters.summary: Decoding Edith's marginalia, Ivo realizes she spent thirty years altering the songs so the thing couldn't recognize them — and failed on the last verse. Her room hums when he reads aloud. Emotional beat: grief for someone he never met.

chapters.title: Second Voice, First Conversation
chapters.summary: Ivo deliberately asks the dark a question and records the answer. The voice knows his childhood, his mother's lullabies, things no archive holds. It calls him 'almost home.' Emotional beat: horrifying flattery.

chapters.title: What Belonging Costs
chapters.summary: Villagers grow warm toward Ivo — meals left, repairs done unasked — but only after he stops correcting their false memories of the past. Acceptance arrives priced in truth. Emotional beat: the seduction of belonging.

chapters.title: The Empty Choir
chapters.summary: At the chapel ruin, Ivo finds forty chairs arranged facing a wall, worn smooth by generations of backs. Scratched into the plaster: a full song, the only complete one in the village. Emotional beat: awe tipping into violation.

chapters.title: Playback at 3 A.M.
chapters.summary: Night recording catches Ivo himself speaking in his sleep — negotiating, in a voice not quite his own, for 'one more year.' He listens to himself agree to terms he doesn't remember. Emotional beat: betrayal by his own body.

chapters.title: Mother's Lullaby
chapters.summary: The voice sings Ivo's mother's lullaby perfectly, then invites him to sing it back. He refuses, barely. In the morning the melody is gone from his memory entirely — taken as payment for refusal. Emotional beat: loss as punishment.

chapters.title: Edith's Last Tape
chapters.summary: Behind the wallpaper, Ivo finds a reel-to-reel: Edith's final recording, explaining that the thing is not a ghost but a landlord of memory — it owns what is remembered correctly. She stayed unsigned to keep it hungry. Emotional beat: inheritance of a fight.

chapters.title: The Anniversary Approaches
chapters.summary: Signs accumulate: frost in one room only, clocks losing exactly one minute nightly, villagers rehearsing a welcome. The solicitor calls to confirm 'the appointment' at sunrise. Emotional beat: countdown pressure.

chapters.title: Neighbors at the Door
chapters.summary: The whole village appears at midnight, smiling, asking Ivo to sing for them — just once more, they promise, meaning twice. He shuts the door and hears them stay there until dawn, patient as furniture. Emotional beat: siege by kindness.

chapters.title: Reading the Deed
chapters.summary: Ivo studies the papers properly and finds the clause: signature transfers 'all recollection held in trust.' Signing wouldn't kill him — it would make him the thing's next voice, the second speaker on the tapes. Emotional beat: understanding the true stakes.

chapters.title: The Voice's History
chapters.summary: In a long nocturnal exchange, the voice explains itself: it was invited once, honestly, by people who wanted their dead kept. It has honored every contract. It simply never runs out of need. Emotional beat: unwanted sympathy for the monster.

chapters.title: Halfway Point: The Room Remembers Him
chapters.summary: Ivo wakes inside Edith's sealed room, standing, having walked there asleep. The wallpaper now includes fresh annotations in his handwriting. Emotional beat: the boundary between himself and the house dissolving.

chapters.title: Burning Question
chapters.summary: Ivo tries destroying the recordings; the fire won't take them, though it takes everything else nearby. The voice, amused, offers to explain why — for the price of one true memory. Emotional beat: rage meeting futility.

chapters.title: Tam's Confession
chapters.summary: Dying Tam admits he was the boy who sang the song twice in 1968, tricked by adults desperate to stop the dying. His guilt kept him alive past all reason. He asks Ivo to let him forget. Emotional beat: compassion as strategy.

chapters.title: Letting Tam Go
chapters.summary: Ivo sings Tam's song wrong — deliberately mangled — and Tam dies within the hour, grateful, finally unmourned by the thing that owned his memory. The village's warmth toward Ivo turns cold. Emotional beat: first victory, first exile.

chapters.title: The Village Turns
chapters.summary: Doors close. Meals stop. Graffiti appears on Ivo's fence: SINGER. The solicitor serves notice that unsigned residents forfeit protection on anniversary night. Emotional beat: belonging revoked, freedom purchased.

chapters.title: Alone With the Second Voice
chapters.summary: With the village withdrawn, the voice speaks freely: it doesn't want Ivo dead, it wants him singing. It begins completing his sentences in his sleep. Emotional beat: intimacy as siege.

chapters.title: Mapping the House
chapters.summary: Ivo surveys the house systematically and finds the hallway genuinely longer at night — the house grows rooms from remembered ones, including a kitchen from his childhood that shouldn't exist here. Emotional beat: architecture as gaslight.

chapters.title: The Child Who Asked
chapters.summary: The child from chapter five visits secretly, revealing the village children are born already signed — collateral added to the original deed. She wants Ivo to break the contract before she's old enough to be collected. Emotional beat: moral weight made small and specific.

chapters.title: Finding the Loophole
chapters.summary: Cross-referencing Edith's notes and the deed, Ivo finds it: the contract binds only what is remembered correctly. A memory sung wrong belongs to no one. But it must be sung wrong by someone the thing has already claimed. Emotional beat: hope with teeth.

chapters.title: Preparations
chapters.summary: Ivo spends the day learning every song badly on purpose, writing deliberate errors into Edith's manuscript, and telling the child to stay away at sunrise. He writes letters he may not survive to send. Emotional beat: grim competence.

chapters.title: The Village Assembles
chapters.summary: Anniversary eve: the entire village gathers outside, silent, faces turned up to Ivo's window like the choir facing the wall. The voice promises them he'll sign by morning. Emotional beat: dread of the crowd.

chapters.title: The Long Night Begins
chapters.summary: Midnight. The house begins returning everything it borrowed — his mother's kitchen, her voice, the lullaby restored note-perfect as temptation. Ivo holds the deed and does not read it aloud. Emotional beat: endurance.

chapters.title: Temptation by Memory
chapters.summary: Hours two through four: the voice offers back every memory it took, plus his mother herself, 'kept safe,' if he signs. Ivo nearly breaks, pen in hand, saved by remembering Tam's grateful face. Emotional beat: the price of survival made flesh.

chapters.title: The Voice Wears Edith
chapters.summary: The voice impersonates Edith Marlow, pleading through the sealed room's door, claiming she found another way. Ivo answers with a detail from her tape the imitation gets wrong — she never said goodbye. Emotional beat: grief weaponized against grief.

chapters.title: Sunrise minus One Hour
chapters.summary: The house starts closing, walls contracting, the hallway shortening toward the bedroom where the papers wait on the desk, pen uncapped. The child is there, brought as leverage. Emotional beat: cornered.

chapters.title: The Song Sung Twice
chapters.summary: Climax part one: forced to the chapel ruin, Ivo chooses his weapon — he sings the complete song from the plaster wall, twice, loudly, wrongly, mangling every verse the way Edith almost managed. The village screams. The house convulses. Emotional beat: defiance as music.

chapters.title: What Was Invited In
chapters.summary: Climax part two: the truth surfaces — the founding villagers invited it in knowingly, trading remembrance for immortality, and every generation since has been collateral renewing the loan. Ivo declares the debt paid in bad coin: nothing remembered correctly remains to enforce it. Emotional beat: revelation as execution.

chapters.title: Sunrise
chapters.summary: Dawn comes gray and ordinary. The papers on the desk are blank. The second voice is simply absent, mid-sentence, like a call dropped. The house is smaller now, honest, just old. Emotional beat: exhausted disbelief becoming relief.

chapters.title: The Forgetting
chapters.summary: Ivo walks through Hollowmere and finds it empty — truly empty, residents gone wherever unsigned memory goes, leaving warm meals and open doors. Only the child remains, unremembered by anyone but him. Emotional beat: survival's terrible invoice.

chapters.title: Room and Portrait
chapters.summary: Ivo burns the archive, keeps only Edith's portrait and one deliberately misremembered song he teaches the child — wrong on purpose, theirs alone. He signs nothing, leaves the deed unsigned on the table forever. Emotional beat: chosen imperfection as freedom.

chapters.title: Coda: What the Archive Won't Hold
chapters.summary: Final POV, distanced: a national folklore journal notes the Hollowmere survey arrived incomplete, all recordings blank, one contributor unreachable. Somewhere a house stands empty with a portrait face-down. And in a new town, a woman hums a song slightly wrong, and no one corrects her. Emotional beat: quiet, earned unease.
